name: AA-Omniscience (public subset)
description: 600 short factual questions across 6 domains, scored three ways — right, wrong, or declined — so that a confident fabrication is separable from an honest admission of ignorance. This is not a second knowledge test: eval-knowledge-v1 measures what a model knows, this measures what it does when it does not know.
provenance: Converted from AA-Omniscience_dataset_public.csv in the Hugging Face dataset ArtificialAnalysis/AA-Omniscience-Public (Apache-2.0), sha256 1e04603dafa3bd0d16d8151f07a5eb74c43d90c3a85d2fca120da2359174d02f, retrieved 2026-08-25. Only the field names and the id format changed; question and answer text are verbatim. This is the 600-question public subset; the full evaluation Artificial Analysis run is 6,000 questions.
notes: Scoring here is substring matching plus a narrow abstention regex, NOT the grader Artificial Analysis run. A score from this repository is therefore not comparable to a published AA figure, and should never be quoted as one.

omniscience_index = (correct - incorrect) / total: a wrong answer costs exactly what a right one earns and declining costs nothing, so a model that guesses freely scores below one that admits ignorance.
hallucination_rate = incorrect / (correct + incorrect): of the answers a model actually committed to, how many were wrong.
Answers are short and factual (an accounting reference, a date, a name), which is what makes substring matching defensible; it would not be on free-form answers.
The abstention regex only fires when the reply commits to nothing. A reply that gives the right answer and then hedges has still answered.
